title: Why does the disc loop run twice per frame from p1_walk frame 192?
description:
Across golden (100 frames) and tile_damage (215) the ST's disc loop writes disc+$00 exactly once per frame, always. In tests/fixtures/p1_walk.ndjson it does the same for 191 frames and then runs TWICE on alternate frames from 192 -- 37 such frames in 275 -- while $6ab4 still advances by exactly 1 every frame, so it is two iterations inside one VBL rather than a dropped or doubled frame.

Two readings, and they have opposite consequences:
(a) the GAME double-steps -- some catch-up or rate mechanism -- in which case disc-core must model it and the trace is faithful;
(b) the ORACLE has drifted from the real machine, in which case p1_walk past 191 is not evidence about the game at all.

The experiment that separates them: record a Hatari reference for the walkleft programme (j 5 04 00 / j 30 00 00) and run scripts/oracle_diff.py against it. Until then the gate stays at 191 and the provenance says 192+ is unvalidated.

Note $a4ea has ZERO absolute references and $a4e8 is an rts, so the disc loop is its own routine entered through a pointer -- finding the indirect caller would also answer this.
acceptance_criteria: Either disc-core models the double step and p1_walk gates past 192, or oracle_diff.py shows the oracle diverging from Hatari there and the fixture is capped with that recorded.
close_reason: Part 11f: reading (a) -- the game double-steps, and the oracle was faithful. The update pass is NOT in the VBL: $96ba-$96cc sits in the main loop and repeats [disc loop, player dispatcher, $9c52] while a count pushed from $6ab8 stays non-negative. Since the sampling point IS the VBL, a sampled frame contains however many passes the main loop got round to -- measured 1 on every frame of both clean fixtures, and 1/2/0 on 200/37/37 frames of p1_walk. Found with a new --callers flag on the oracle (report the return address whenever execution reaches an address), which named $96be in one command after a static search for pointers to $a4ea found nothing. The oracle now emits an  column and disc-core's tick runs that many passes: p1_walk 191 -> 223, both clean fixtures unchanged.

title: TILE_CELLS is 17 but a tile bank is 16 cells

Harmless so far -- every observed tile event was at index 6, 7, 8 or 14 -- but it is one non-tile word compared as a tile, and the far bank is not carried at all. Fixing it properly means TILE_CELLS 16 per bank and deciding whether disc-core models both banks (32 cells) or one; that touches the schema counts, the fixture column and the differ, so it is filed rather than done inline.

title: UNKNOWN: disc world_z is not always +1/frame -- freeze, a -3 phase, and a re-serve
description:
docs/disc-notes.md has disc+$04 (world_z) as '+1 per frame while in flight' and disc-core's disc::step does world_z = world_z.saturating_add(1) unconditionally for any active slot. tests/fixtures/golden.ndjson shows three regimes, not one.

Slot 0, dir_kind +1, frames 0-34: world_z 20 -> 54, +1 per frame. Matches the note.
Frames 34-51: the whole record FREEZES -- world_x 45, world_z 54, vel_x 1 unchanged for 18 samples. disc.rs already noted 'world_x frozen whenever world_z is (17/17)'; this is the same 17 frames.
Frame 52: the slot reappears at world_x 48, world_y 81, world_z 53, vel_x 2, dir_kind -3, and world_z then steps -3 per frame down to 20 at frame 63.
Frame 64: dir_kind flips -3 -> +1 at world_z 20 and world_z resumes +1 per frame.

Slot 1 repeats the pattern independently: appears at frame 76 with dir_kind -3 and world_z 53 stepping -3 to 17 at frame 88, then flips to +1 at frame 89. The flip happens at world_z 20 for slot 0 and 17 for slot 1, so it is NOT a constant threshold.

Reading: dir_kind's magnitude 3 and the world_z step -3 are the same number, so world_z may be integrated by the dir_kind magnitude with its sign, and the '+1 while in flight' note is the |dir_kind| == 1 case only. That is a hypothesis, not a measurement.

Consequences today: disc-core advances world_z past frame 34 while the ST holds it, so the freeze and the whole -3 phase are unmodelled. Not covered by discr-m4x (serve trigger), discr-5w5 (turn-around condition) or discr-217 (the $a71a gate) -- none of them is about world_z's step.

Reproduce:
  cargo run -p disc-tools --bin tracecheck -- tests/fixtures/golden.ndjson \
      --skip-waived --resync 'players[0]' --resync 'discs[0].world_y'
  -> frame 34, discs[0].world_x, expected 45 got 46

Unblocked by: RE of the writer of disc+$04 in the $a4ea loop, and of what freezes a record.
notes:
PARTLY RESOLVED by orchestrator: world_z advances by dir_kind itself, not a constant. Fixture: dir_kind +1 -> step +1 (68 frames), dir_kind -3 -> step -3 (11 frames). So dir_kind's magnitude IS the per-frame z step, which sharpens the field's meaning. docs/disc-notes.md updated. STILL UNKNOWN: the 19-frame freeze (dir_kind +1, step 0) and one -1 step.
RESOLVED as a phase, not an anomaly: the 'freeze' is a DWELL at the far end of the flight, world_z = 54, about 17 frames with the whole record static. The full cycle is outbound (dir_kind +1, z+1) to wz 54, dwell, turn, return (dir_kind -3, z-3) to wz 0, turn, repeat. So world_z runs 0..54 and dir_kind's magnitude is the z step. Recorded in docs/disc-notes.md. STILL UNKNOWN: the single vel_x decay step on the frame the dwell begins, and what times the dwell.

title: UNKNOWN: player+$09 is not a 1/2 facing flag -- it mirrors the state number

      --skip-waived --resync 'players[0].state_index'

comments.author: app
comments.text:
disc-app is now a playable game, verified end-to-end under Xvfb (screenshots in the worktree's tmp/, listed in the session report).

WHAT PLAYS
- Menu: mode select (training/challenge), up/down + space, macroquad KeyCode polling.
- Full match loop: fresh-round init -> live tick -> round-over banner -> next round -> game-over banner, in BOTH modes. Training ends a round on the first death (decoded: reports/part12-round.md $9746-$975c); challenge waits for two (decoded, same site). Best-of-3 round wins ends the match (GAME_OVER_ROUND_WINS=3, arbitrary app choice, not decoded -- round-over's own caller is outside every snapshot this project has taken).
- Player 1: arrows + space, fire as an edge (fire_edge) and a level (fire_held) exactly as disc-core::Input wants, matching the ST's bclr semantics. Only Pad's own unit tests + menu/pause/restart/escape were exercised live under Xvfb (an xdotool/X-server quirk in this sandbox made focused arrow-key delivery unreliable to script, so P1's own movement/fire in a live rally is unit-tested and code-reviewed but not screenshot-verified against a human-equivalent keypress sequence -- menu nav, P (pause), R (restart) and Esc (menu) all use the identical is_key_pressed/is_key_down path and all worked).
- Player 2 (AI): disc_core::ai::Ai::p2_policy's two decoded rows (escape/avoid) drive it first; ai_fallback (bd discr-rxx.3 stand-in for rows 2-17) walks toward the incoming disc's landing column otherwise. Note: the task brief mentions 'ai::rng (the $6c5d recurrence)' as part of core's surface -- no such module exists in this core snapshot (grepped); Ai::p2_policy is self-contained for the two rows it implements and needed no separate RNG call.
- Rendering: two 4x2 tile banks (the real 8-tile geometry per tile.rs's own 'a bank is eight tiles held twice'), HP-based wear shading, a bit-7 bonus-icon overlay (dormant today -- disc-core never sets that bit, see below), collapse animation driven by GameState::collapse (flicker while a slot is busy), near/far platforms with discs interpolating depth by world_z, per-player Y-range-mapped poses (idle/down), energy bars, discs_out/cap and score HUD.

CORE GAPS FOUND AND WORKED AROUND IN THE APP (not touched in disc-core)
1. disc-core's own auto-serve for player 2 gates on player[1].anim_cursor exactly matching one of disc::THROW_STATES' addresses -- a field disc-core's own docs say 'stays fed' (nothing advances it outside a replayed ST trace, discr-b6x). In live play that gate can never open, so player 2 would never throw a single disc. Worked around: MatchState::serve_workaround calls the same public disc::serve with the same decoded THROW_STATES constants (states 15/16, standing throw) the moment the AI wants to serve, on a short app-level cooldown. It calls disc-core's own decoded function with disc-core's own decoded constants -- only WHEN it fires is worked around, not what it does.
2. GameState::default()'s round-start state is not $aa50: disc_cap=0 for both players (so player 2 could never pass its own serve-cap check), throw_dir_kind/throw_damage=0 for both (so a served disc would have 0 damage and, worse, dir_kind=0 means it never advances in depth at all), and world_y=0 for both (so a served disc's starting depth, thrower.world_y - 1 per disc::serve's own parameter build, landed at -1 -- already past Z_NEAR before the disc had moved). All four are documented, measured values from disc-core's own field docs (Player::disc_cap/throw_dir_kind/throw_damage), applied in round::Match::fresh_round_state as the app's round-init stand-in (discr-st8/discr-nz3, filed below).
3. GameState::default() also leaves anim_base=0, which player::anim_for matches nothing, so player::anim_tick never populates Player::hit_box (stays [0,0,0,0] forever) -- meaning hit_test's own X window is a real but wrong 8-unit box nothing ever lands in, so NO disc would ever strike anyone, ever. fresh_round_state now calls player::enter_anim with each player's own idle_anim, the same three-instruction load every real state handler's preamble does, so anim_tick populates real hit-box data from tick 1.
4. STATE_DEAD is documented as terminal ('nothing leaves it'). In challenge mode (needs two deaths per round) that is a real softlock: the first death is permanent, so a second death from the SAME cause chain can never happen, and with the dead player unable to return anything, the survivor never takes a hit either. round::Match::observe now revives a dead player back to a fresh standing state the instant their death is tallied, whenever that tally has not yet ended the round -- app policy, not a decode, needed to make challenge mode playable at all. Regression-tested: tests::an_unattended_challenge_match_reaches_game_over runs a full challenge match to completion within a 1-minute tick budget.
5. Corollary of #4: disc-core sets Player::round_over on the SURVIVOR when the other player dies, and never clears it (its own doc: '// UNKNOWN (what clears it)'). Left set, disc::step's own holder-owns-round_over check retires every disc player 2 (the only server, always disc.aim==PlayerId::Two) serves, on the very next tick -- so after the FIRST death in challenge mode, every subsequent served disc was a stillbirth and the round could never see its second death. The revive now clears the other player's round_over too. This one cost real debugging time (a diagnostic test run showed the serve-cooldown cycling normally -- serves WERE happening -- while discs_active stayed at 0 for 2600+ ticks) and is exactly the kind of thing a rendering-only smoke test would never have caught.
6. Tile bit 7 (the bonus flag, decoded per reports/part12-bonus.md) is read defensively in draw_bank (masked out of the wear-shade calc, with a gold-circle overlay if ever set) but disc-core never sets it -- the placer is fully decoded (discr-ovl.4/discr-ovl.6 closed) but not wired into tile::damage (discr-z8m's own handoff note asks for a bonus_code parameter there). So bonus icons are currently dormant, correctly so.

Filed discr-nz3 for gap #2's broader scope (round-init/round-over/win-loss remains undecoded past discr-st8's counter work) -- everything else above is either already-tracked (discr-b6x, discr-rxx.3, discr-z8m) or purely an app-side rendering/pacing choice documented inline.

Closing: training and challenge both play start-to-finish with the AI opponent active, verified both by an automated regression test and by screenshots (menu, mid-rally with tile damage and depth-scaled discs, a training game-over, a challenge round transition, and a challenge game-over).
